subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw preserve strong `message_tool_only` guidance in stable prompt/schema surfaces, or move that guidance into late per-turn content to prioritize OpenAI prefix-cache reuse?
rationale: The source-level churn is clear, but the durable fix affects delivery reliability, tool schema wording, and provider-specific prompt-cache behavior, so maintainer intent should choose the owner boundary before automation changes prompt contracts.

options.title: Move Guidance Late
options.body: Move turn-specific `message_tool_only` instructions out of the stable system prompt and message tool description into current-turn context while keeping delivery enforcement unchanged.

options.title: Make Mode Session-Stable
options.body: Keep strong guidance in prompt/schema only when the delivery mode is stable for that conversation, avoiding alternating per-turn prompt bytes.

options.title: Document And Accept Churn
options.body: Keep the current prompt/schema guidance and document the expected OpenAI cache cost and latency tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Move Guidance Late
recommendation.body: Move turn-specific `message_tool_only` instructions out of the stable system prompt and message tool description into current-turn context while keeping delivery enforcement unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work already split effective per-turn and session-stable source reply delivery facts across the adjacent prompt-binding path.
